name: semantic-crosscheck
description: Cross-layer verification for an ontology plus semantic layer on PostgreSQL 17, for Codex and Claude Code.

interface.shortDescription: Prove that a PostgreSQL closure, SHACL rules, OWL reasoning and a Cube model agree.
interface.longDescription: Release v0.19.1: validate complete saved-result/check structures and live SHACL report envelopes before accepting evidence. Valid legacy unversioned results remain supported; new results declare schema version1. Malformed evidence cannot pass by dropping entries, including optional stale stages. Warning/info handling and valid cross-group SHACL projection retain their documented semantics. The opt-in offline boundary-schema command derives exact integer, numeric(p,s) or date neighbors from one declared scalar comparison and emits an existing witness-v1 schema. It is a fully consuming restricted grammar, not a PostgreSQL parser, SQL sandbox, query-equivalence proof or automatic correspondence to caller SQL. Opt-in TLP/NoREC reduction reuses structured shrinking and replays bound original/accepted/final observations; its signature preserves a declared discrepancy scope, not the same optimizer bug or global minimality. The default pipeline, runtime/dependency pins and report authority are unchanged. Existing exact Cube JSON, Gold metadata and bounded HTTP contracts remain in force. No new PostgreSQL extension, model call, installed-plugin update or company database verification is introduced. Rerun operational stages after upgrading.
defaultPrompt: Use semantic-crosscheck to run the synthetic demo end to end.
Use semantic-crosscheck to verify my crosscheck.toml against PostgreSQL and explain what is not proven.
